findings.title: deleteCache throws plain Error instead of TRPCError and ignores non-user credentials
findings.body: The handler looks up the credential with `userId: user.id` only and throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` when not found. A plain Error surfaces to tRPC as an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, so the client cannot distinguish auth failure from a real server error and the error is logged as an unexpected exception. It should throw `TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" | "FORBIDDEN" })`. Additionally, credentials owned by a team/organization or delegation credentials (userId null or different owner) can never be cleared through this endpoint even though the UI shows the action.

findings.title: Cache deletion does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: On successful `deleteCache`, only the optional `onSuccess` callback is invoked; unlike the disconnect mutation (which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in onSettled), no query invalidation happens. Since `connectedCalendars` is fetched with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, the dropdown continues to show the old "Last updated" timestamp and the delete option after the cache was deleted, until a full reload. Add `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` on settle.

findings.title: Cache status never resolves for delegation credentials
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` queries CalendarCache by `credentialId`, but in-memory delegation credentials have synthetic negative ids and their cache rows are looked up by `userId` only (see getCachedAvailability's isInMemoryDelegationCredential branch). For delegation-based connections `cacheUpdatedAt` will therefore always be null and the UI will claim there is no cache even when one exists.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId with empty data on every cache refresh
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` issues an UPDATE on every selected calendar of the credential each time availability is cached, solely to bump `updatedAt`. This value is not consumed anywhere in the UI (the UI uses CalendarCache.updatedAt), so it is a write amplification on a hot path (webhook handling / cron cache refresh) with no consumer. It also touches rows for calendars not involved in the refresh, and is a no-op for delegation credentials with negative ids. Either remove it or restrict it to the calendars actually refreshed.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` ignores the user's locale/time format preference, so the "Last updated" timestamp is always rendered in US format (and 12h clock) regardless of the user's selected language or timeFormat setting. Use the locale from `useLocale()` / the user's timeFormat.

findings.title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and ENV_FILE path is relative to cwd
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` fails on Linux with GNU sed, which interprets the empty string as the input filename ("can't read : No such file or directory"), so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated for Linux contributors. Also `ENV_FILE="../.env"` resolves relative to the caller's working directory, so running the script from the repo root writes/creates a `.env` outside the repository.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to npx tsx without adding tsx as a dependency
findings.body: `"dev:cron": "npx tsx cron-tester.ts"` relies on `npx` fetching `tsx` from the network at runtime since `tsx` is not listed in dependencies/devDependencies (while the now-unused `ts-node` remains). This breaks offline/CI usage and pins no version. Add `tsx` as a devDependency (and drop ts-node if unused).

findings.title: Migration warning comment contradicts the actual statement
findings.body: The generated warning says the column is added "without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty", but the statement does add `DEFAULT NOW()`. Leaving the stale warning is misleading to reviewers/operators evaluating migration safety; it should be removed or corrected.

findings.title: No tests for new deleteCache handler or cache status enrichment
findings.body: The new mutation performs a destructive `calendarCache.deleteMany` based on a user-supplied credentialId, and `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` feeds UI state, yet neither has unit tests covering authorization rejection (credential belonging to another user), deletion scope, or the credentialId→updatedAt mapping. Given the authorization-sensitive nature of the endpoint, tests should be added.
